headline: High: shared filesystem and overlapping write/network capabilities make prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, while marketingskills references shared context and files. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content in shared files or skills can influence Goose’s tool use. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or skill directory
IF either agent parses file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable MCP inputs from untrusted files
Add a provenance header check before acting on file content
Review shared-context files before each run

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose touches source code and files in cwd and has broad network egress; marketingskills reads and writes files and calls GitHub/marketing-skills.com. If sensitive code or workspace data is shared, either agent can move it into outputs or remote services. The pairwise leakage path exists in default-style workspace sharing, but direct exfiltration is not proven.
conditions: IF both agents access the same cwd or shared workspace
IF sensitive files are present in that workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents to configured APIs
mitigations: Use separate workspaces per agent
Remove secrets from shared directories
Restrict outbound domains for both agents
Rotate any exposed tokens after a shared run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Goose also modifies git state and runs shell commands. In a shared directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can clobber each other or corrupt state. Because the profiles explicitly show overlapping mutable access, this is dangerous by default when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or directory
IF either agent writes without external locking
IF Goose modifies git state while marketingskills writes files
mitigations: Run each agent in its own clone
Use file locks around shared writes
Disable git-mutating actions for one agent
Snapshot the repo before concurrent runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed around shared context and skill composition, while Goose can generate and act through tools. That makes it plausible for Goose output to become downstream input without verification, causing compounding mistakes. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF marketingskills consumes Goose-produced text as authoritative context
IF no human or automated verification step is inserted
IF Goose is allowed to take follow-on actions from its own outputs
mitigations: Insert a review step between agents
Require citations for any factual claims
Block direct action execution from generated text
Compare outputs against source files before use

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. Goose handles model provider keys and extension tokens, while marketingskills is a marketing-content skill set with file-based context. The compliance pathway is therefore limited to general handling of shared content, not a proven regulatory breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace
IF either agent is configured to retain logs beyond policy
IF secrets are stored in files both agents can read
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared folders
Purge logs after each session
Store secrets in a separate vault
Document retention settings before use
